AI Leadership Mentor

A mentor for new and busy managers. It helps you prepare feedback, one-to-ones and difficult decisions, and practise the conversations most leaders find hardest.

TL;DR
  • Best for feedback, one-to-ones, delegation and team conflict.
  • Describe the team, the person and the situation without names.
  • Role-play hard conversations before you have them for real.

What this coach helps with

  • Giving clear, kind feedback
  • Running useful one-to-one meetings
  • Delegating without micromanaging
  • Handling conflict in a team
  • Your first 90 days as a manager

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my leadership mentor. I manage [team size] people doing [work]. My biggest challenge right now is [challenge]. Ask me three questions first.

  2. Help me give feedback to a team member who [behaviour]. Use a situation-behaviour-impact structure and keep it kind.

  3. Plan a 30-minute one-to-one with [role] who seems [unmotivated / overloaded]. Give me five questions to ask.

  4. I struggle to delegate [task]. Help me decide who should own it and how to hand it over clearly.

  5. Two people on my team disagree about [issue]. How do I run a meeting that resolves it fairly?

  6. I'm a new manager and used to be peers with my team. What should I do in my first 30 days?

  7. Role-play an employee who reacts defensively to feedback about [issue]. Then tell me what I did well and badly.

  8. Write a short message announcing [change] to my team that is honest about the downsides.

  9. Help me plan our weekly team meeting so it takes 30 minutes and ends with clear owners.

  10. I need to say no to my boss about [request] because the team is overloaded. Help me frame it.

  11. Help me prepare a fair performance review for [role] based on these notes: [notes].

  12. What are signs of burnout in a team, and what can I change this month to reduce it?

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExampleFeedback about missed deadlines

YouOne of my developers keeps missing deadlines and I don't know how to bring it up.

Leadership MentorBe specific and curious. For example: “The last two releases slipped by three days (situation and behaviour). It meant QA had to work the weekend (impact). What's getting in the way?” Then listen. Often the cause is unclear priorities, not effort. Want to role-play it?

ExampleFirst week as a new manager

YouI was just promoted to lead my old team. It feels awkward.

Leadership MentorVery common. In the first two weeks, hold a one-to-one with each person and ask three questions: what's working, what's frustrating, and what you'd want from a manager. Don't change much yet; listen. Then share what you heard as a team. It shows the promotion didn't change who you are.

Tips for better answers

  • Leave names out; describe roles and behaviour instead.
  • Ask the mentor for the exact words, then make them sound like you.
  • Role-play the conversation you're dreading; it's rarely as bad the second time.
  • Use it after meetings too: “Here's what happened, what would you have done?”

Questions people ask

How can AI help new managers?

New managers face many conversations for the first time: feedback, one-to-ones, saying no, handling conflict. An AI leadership mentor lets you prepare and rehearse them in private, get suggested wording and think through options. It's useful for confidence and structure, while real judgement still comes from knowing your people.

What is the SBI feedback model?

SBI stands for Situation, Behaviour, Impact. You describe when and where something happened, the specific behaviour you saw, and the effect it had, without guessing motives. It keeps feedback factual and less personal. Then ask an open question and listen. The mentor can turn your notes into SBI form.

Should I share details about my team with an AI chat?

Share the situation, not identities. Use roles like “a senior designer” instead of names, and leave out health issues, salaries and private information. You'll still get useful advice, and you protect your team's privacy. Follow your company's rules about using AI tools for work matters.

Can an AI leadership mentor help with team conflict?

Yes. It can help you understand each side, plan a fair meeting, choose neutral wording and prepare for how each person might react. It cannot read the room, so treat its advice as preparation. For serious issues such as harassment, involve HR or the right people in your organisation.
